item.title: Araghchi meets Spanish FM calls for European action against US aggression
item.description: Seyed Abbas Araghchi, Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Islamic Republic of Iran, who is in New York to attend the annual session of the United Nations General Assembly, met and held talks with José Manuel Albares Bueno, Minister of Foreign Affairs of Spain, on Thursday morning. The Iranian Foreign Minister, outlining the ongoing developments in the West Asia region, stressed the importance of European countries adopting a responsible approach consistent with international law toward the US aggressive and unlawful actions against Iran. The Foreign Minister also, referring to the continued occupation and genocide of the Palestinians and Israel’s aggressive expansionism in the region, underscored the responsibility of all states to stop these acts of aggression and hold the Zionist perpetrators accountable and punish them. The two sides also discussed and exchanged views on bilateral relations between Iran and Spain.

item.title: Iran Poland FMs discuss regional developments Ukraine conflict
item.description: Iranian Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi, who is in New York to attend the annual session of the United Nations General Assembly, met with Polish Foreign Minister Radosław Sikorski on Thursday morning. Araghchi outlined Iran’s positions on developments in West Asia, saying that the insecurity in the Strait of Hormuz stems from US acts of aggression. He stressed the importance of all countries, including European states, adopting a principled position in condemning the military aggression against Iran as well as the crimes committed during it. The Iranian foreign minister also expressed concern over the continuation of the Ukraine conflict, describing as highly dangerous attempts by some parties to shift blame and link the conflict to developments in West Asia. He stressed the importance of European countries dealing responsibly with issues concerning their continent. The two sides also discussed and exchanged views on Iran-Poland bilateral relations.

item.title: Iran Jordan FMs meet in New York discuss regional security bilateral ties
item.description: Iranian Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi, who has traveled to New York to attend the annual session of the United Nations General Assembly, met with Jordanian Foreign Minister Ayman Safadi on Thursday morning. Araghchi, referring to Iran’s principled position of respecting the national sovereignty and territorial integrity of all countries in the region, described the use of some countries’ territories as sites for planning and carrying out US and Israeli military aggression as regrettable. He stressed Iran’s readiness to engage with all regional countries to strengthen trust and cooperation on mechanisms for endogenous regional security. Araghchi described the issue of Palestine as the most important issue facing the Muslim world and the international community, stressing the need for cooperation among Islamic countries and more serious action by the Organization of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) to end the Israeli regime’s impunity and halt its occupation, genocide and expansionism. The two sides also exchanged views on Iran-Jordan bilateral relations and cooperation.

Seyed Abbas Araghchi, Foreign Minister of the Islamic Republic of Iran, who has traveled to New York to attend the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly, met with Mohammad Ishaq Dar, Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister of Pakistan, on Wednesday evening as part of his consultations with countries participating in the session. The two sides discussed and exchanged views on bilateral relations and the most important regional and international developments. The foreign ministers of Iran and Pakistan reviewed the latest developments in bilateral relations and reaffirmed the two countries’ determination to pursue the implementation of their agreements and further expand relations within the framework of mutual interests. The Iranian Foreign Minister expressed appreciation for Pakistan’s constructive efforts as a mediator in the negotiations with the United States, saying that the repeated breaches of commitments by the United States had undermined the position of the mediating institution. He stressed that the US violation of the Islamabad understanding had resulted in heightened insecurity and tensions in the region, and that the United States is responsible for the continuation of the consequences of this situation. Araghchi briefed his Pakistani counterpart on the latest status of the talks and bilateral understanding between Iran and Oman regarding the determination of an appropriate route for the safe passage of vessels through the Strait of Hormuz, as well as the interactions with the United States through Qatar. Araghchi also, referring to the continuation of the genocide against Palestinians and the ever-expanding occupation by the Israeli regime in the occupied Palestinian territories, called for serious action by Islamic countries and the Organization of Islamic Cooperation to assist the Palestinian people and counter the crimes of the Israeli regime. The Pakistani Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister, for his part, stressed his country’s particular commitment to continuing its good offices, together with other countries in the region, to help establish peace and stability in the region.

item.title: Iran Ukraine FMs sgree to maintain contacts to prevent further tensions
item.description: Following a telephone conversation between the foreign ministers of Iran and Ukraine in August, Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha met with Iranian Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi on the sidelines of the high-level session of the United Nations General Assembly in New York. During the meeting, the two sides stressed the importance of diplomacy in managing tensions. The foreign ministers of the two countries also deemed it necessary to maintain channels of communication between the two countries and emphasized the need to take the necessary bilateral steps to manage their relations. The two sides also exchanged views on developments in Europe and the West Asia region and agreed to continue their contacts with the aim of preventing any escalation of tensions in their relations. The two sides also exchanged views on bilateral issues, particularly the illegal attack on an Iranian vessel in the Caspian Sea, as well as ways to resolve these issues.

item.title: Iranian South Korean FMs discuss bilateral ties in meeting in New York
item.description: Seyed Abbas Araghchi, Foreign Minister of the Islamic Republic of Iran, and Cho Hyun, Foreign Minister of the Republic of Korea, met and held talks on the sidelines of the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly in New York. The two sides exchanged views on Tehran-Seoul bilateral relations and ways to strengthen ties and cooperation. They also discussed developments in West Asia and on the Korean Peninsula. The Iranian Foreign Minister, referring to the insecurity imposed on the Strait of Hormuz as a result of the aggressive actions of the United States and the Israeli regime, stressed the importance of a responsible and realistic approach by all countries and avoiding any action that could be construed as contributing to the illegal and aggressive activities of the United States in the region. During the meeting, the two foreign ministers also signed a memorandum of understanding on the transfer of sentenced persons between the two countries.

item.title: Iranian Tajik FMs meet in New York discuss bilateral ties regional developments
item.description: Seyed Abbas Araghchi, Foreign Minister of the Islamic Republic of Iran, who has traveled to New York to attend the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly, met with Sirojiddin Muhriddin, Foreign Minister of the Republic of Tajikistan, at noon on Wednesday as part of his consultations with countries participating in the session. They discussed bilateral relations and the most important developments in Central Asia, the Caucasus and West Asia. Referring to the historical, civilizational, cultural and linguistic ties between the two nations, Araghchi stressed the Islamic Republic of Iran’s determination to develop and deepen relations with Tajikistan in all areas of mutual interest. Araghchi also, while explaining the latest regional developments following the US and Israeli regime’s military aggression against Iran and the continuation of economic terrorism and the naval blockade, stressed that the Iranian nation remains steadfast and determined in defending Iran’s existence and sovereignty. The two sides also held consultations on the implementation of the understandings reached between the two countries in various economic and trade fields.

Seyed Abbas Araghchi, Foreign Minister of the Islamic Republic of Iran, who has traveled to New York to attend the annual session of the United Nations General Assembly, met and held talks with Johann Wadephul, German Foreign Minister, on Wednesday morning on the sidelines of the session. The two sides discussed and exchanged views on Iran-Germany bilateral relations as well as regional and international issues. The Iranian Foreign Minister, while outlining the Islamic Republic of Iran’s positions regarding international developments, said that restoring confidence in the functioning of the United Nations requires all states to adhere to the principles and purposes of the UN Charter and international law. He criticized the conduct of European countries, including Germany, for their appeasement in the face of US lawlessness and bullying. The Foreign Minister also, referring to the continuation of the Israeli regime’s occupation and warmongering in the West Asia region, described the military and political support provided by Germany and some other European countries as a major factor in the continuation of the regime’s crimes against countries in the region. He stressed the need to end such complicity in crimes, put an end to impunity, and hold the occupying regime accountable. The Foreign Minister, also explaining Iran’s responsible approach in resorting to diplomacy regarding Iran’s peaceful nuclear program, stressed that no party can ignore Iran’s goodwill in the negotiations and the US and Israeli regime’s military aggression against Iran in the midst of the talks, and portray Iran as the cause of insecurity in the Strait of Hormuz. The Foreign Minister stressed that the Islamic Republic of Iran has conveyed to the US side the rational conditions and elements necessary for advancing diplomacy, emphasizing that restoring security to the region requires an end to US interventionist and aggressive actions against Iran. The two sides also discussed and exchanged views on bilateral relations as well as diplomatic and consular consultations between the two countries.
